review_note: At duality.tex line 4369 the pinned source has a COMMUTATIVE, not necessarily cartesian, open-immersion square of FTS_S schemes and equality j* f^! ≅ g^! j'^* on D_QCoh^+. The reconstruction retains exactly these weaker square hypotheses and derives the naturally isomorphic functors without silently requiring a fibre product.
statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For any commutative square $U\xrightarrow jX$, $V\xrightarrow{j'}Y$ with vertical arrows $g:U\to V$ and $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, where $j$ and $j'$ are open immersions and $f\circ j=j'\circ g$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism of functors
\[
j^*\circ f^!\xrightarrow{\sim}g^!\circ(j')^*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_U).
\]
The square is not required to be cartesian: the result follows from composition coherence and $j^!\cong j^*$ for open immersions.
hypotheses: Noetherian S, commutative square in FTS_S, horizontal maps open immersions.
conclusions: Restricting before or after upper shriek gives naturally isomorphic functors.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-restrict-before-or-after}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[r]_j \ar[d]_g & X \ar[d]^f \\
V \ar[r]^{j'} & Y
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of $\textit{FTS}_S$ where $j$ and $j'$ are
open immersions. Then $j^* \circ f^! = g^! \circ (j')^*$ as functors
$D^+_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to D^+(\mathcal{O}_U)$.

statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. If $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed immersion in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, then for each $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ there is a functorial isomorphism
\[
i^!(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_X(\mathcal O_X,K),
\]
where $R\mathcal Hom_X(\mathcal O_X,-)$ denotes the *exact-support* derived right adjoint to $Ri_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$; its pushforward is $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(i_*\mathcal O_X,K)$, and on affines $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $B=A/I$ it is the sheafification of $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,-)$ with its natural $B$-module structure.
hypotheses: i closed immersion in FTS_S; K bounded-below D_QCoh.
conclusions: The upper-shriek functor for a closed immersion equals derived exact-support Hom.

statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, an object $D\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is a *dualizing complex* if on every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ it is the sheafification of a ring-theoretic dualizing complex: a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D_A,D_A)$. Write $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^\pm,D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b$ for derived complexes with coherent bounded-below, bounded-above and bounded cohomology respectively. If $f:X\to Y$ lies in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, then its upper-shriek functor maps bounded-below complexes with coherent cohomology to bounded-below complexes with coherent cohomology:
\[
f^!:D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_X).
\]
The assertion does not extend automatically to the unbounded-right-adjoint $a_f$ without a proper compactification.
hypotheses: f separated finite-type S-morphism between FTS_S objects.
conclusions: Upper shriek preserves bounded-below coherent-derived complexes.

Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, an object $D\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is a *dualizing complex* if on every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ it is the sheafification of a ring-theoretic dualizing complex: a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D_A,D_A)$. Write $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^\pm,D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b$ for derived complexes with coherent bounded-below, bounded-above and bounded cohomology respectively. Let $K$ be dualizing on $Y$ and put $K_X=f^!K$ (dualizing on $X$). For $M\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ set $\mathbb D_Y(M)=R\mathcal Hom_Y(M,K)$, and for $E\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ set $\mathbb D_X(E)=R\mathcal Hom_X(E,K_X)$. Then for every *bounded-below coherent* $M\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ there is a canonical functorial isomorphism
\[
f^!M\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb D_X(Lf^*\mathbb D_Y(M)).
\]
The derived pullback is essential, and its input may be unbounded above; the right side is interpreted in the appropriate coherent-derived setting under these hypotheses.
hypotheses: f in FTS_S; K dualizing on Y, and M bounded-below coherent-derived.
conclusions: Upper shriek is computed by dualizing, pulling back, and dualizing again.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-shriek-via-duality}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $K$ be a dualizing complex
on $Y$. Set $D_Y(M) = R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_Y}(M, K)$ for
$M \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ and
$D_X(E) = R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(E, f^!K)$ for
$E \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$. Then there is a canonical
isomorphism
$$
f^!M \longrightarrow D_X(Lf^*D_Y(M))
$$
for $M \in D_{\textit{Coh}}^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.

The draft retains ALL five scopes, including no coherence restriction on K in (e).
statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}f^!\mathcal O_Y\to f^!K$ be the *upper-shriek projection comparison*, induced from the projection formula and the adjunction counit on a proper compactification, then restricted to the open $X$. Assume $f$ is a *perfect morphism* (finite Tor-dimension with the usual pseudo-coherence condition, e.g. a flat morphism of finite presentation). Then (a) $f^!\mathcal O_Y\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$; (b) $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ has finite Tor dimension over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$; (c) $\mathcal O_X\to R\mathcal Hom_X(f^!\mathcal O_Y,f^!\mathcal O_Y)$ is an isomorphism; (d) $f^!$ maps $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_Y)$ into $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$; and (e) the canonical upper-shriek comparison
\[
\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}f^!\mathcal O_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}f^!K
\]
is an isomorphism for *all* bounded-below $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ (not necessarily coherent).
hypotheses: f perfect in FTS_S; μ comparison defined using compactification.
conclusions: Five coherence, relative-Tor, homothety, boundedness and projection-comparison properties.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-perfect-comparison-shriek}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Assume $f$ is perfect (e.g., flat). Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ is in $D_{\textit{Coh}}^b(\mathcal{O}_X)$,
\item[(b)] $f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ has finite tor dimension in
$D(f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_Y)$,
\item[(c)] $\mathcal{O}_X \to
R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y, f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)$
is an isomorphism,
\item[(d)] $f^!$ maps $D_{\textit{Coh}}^b(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ into
$D_{\textit{Coh}}^b(\mathcal{O}_X)$,
\item[(e)] the map
$\mu_{f,  K} :
Lf^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} f^!\mathcal{O}_Y
\to
f^!K$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-map-pullback-to-shriek-well-defined}
is an isomorphism for all $K \in D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
\end{enumerate}

statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ is flat. An object $P\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ is *$Y$-perfect* if it is pseudo-coherent and has locally bounded Tor-amplitude relative to $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$. Then $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is $Y$-perfect and the homothety map
\[
\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(f^!\mathcal O_Y,f^!\mathcal O_Y)
\]
is an isomorphism. Flatness here is part of a finite-type morphism in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$.
conclusions: Relative perfectness and derived self-duality of the upper-shriek structure complex.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-shriek-relatively-perfect}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. If $f$ is flat, then
$f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ is a $Y$-perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and
$\mathcal{O}_X \to
R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y, f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)$
is an isomorphism.

statement: Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ is a *local complete intersection morphism*: locally on its source it factors as a regular (Koszul-regular) closed immersion into a smooth $Y$-scheme. Then (1) $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is *derived-invertible*: locally on $X$ it is a shift of an invertible sheaf and admits a two-sided inverse for derived tensor product; and (2) the upper-shriek functor $f^!$ takes perfect objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ to perfect objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, interpreted on the bounded-below subcategory where $f^!$ is defined.
hypotheses: f local complete intersection in FTS_S.
conclusions: Upper-shriek structure complex invertible and f^! preserves perfect complexes.
